D.treatment: presentation of the pedagogical design principles

O.outcome_detail: participants' agreement that the principles foster learning and motivation towards STEM

result.effect: 94.34% agreed or strongly agreed; 50% agreed and 44.34% strongly agreed

cells.quote: In focus group 2, after presenting the pedagogical framework created based on the feedback from focus group 1, 94.34% of all the participants (n = 137) in focus group 2 either agreed (50%) or strongly agreed (44.34%) with the statement, “the presented pedagogical design principles foster learning and motivation towards STEM”.
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive member-check survey, not a treatment-versus-comparison experiment. The comparison is therefore only the remaining disagree/strongly-disagree responses, and no inferential test, confidence interval, or adequate-power claim is reported.

cells.quote: We did not detect any impact on the hard outcomes at the end of the school year, namely: students’ failure, final marks in several subjects and truancies rate.
cells.note: The study states that the trial was powered enough to detect impacts; no effect size is printed.

O.outcome_detail: parental involvement as perceived by students

cells.quote: At the end of the first year, the intervention show ed to be effective on four outcomes: it increased parental involvement (as perceived by stu dents), it reduced their perception of teachers’ hostility and it improved their self-effi cacy about learning and improved their satisfaction about their school experience. All the se effects are statistically and substantially significant (p-value< 0.05 and effect size>.20).
cells.note: The study reports individual-level random assignment of 131 students to treatment and 131 to control; only 84 assigned treatment students accepted the intervention.
